sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Vandu language'; Wikipedia (fr) 'Gelao rouge' (phoneme inventory of Malipo Red Gelao after Li & Han 2009: 4 tones 55/33/35/31); Glottolog 5.x redg1235 page.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent; used only for bibliography and identity.

sources.citation: 李锦芳、艾杰瑞 (Li Jinfang & Jerold A. Edmondson). 2006. 中越边境的红仡佬语及其初步比较. Paper for 民族语言国际学术研讨会, Lijiang, 24-26 Sept 2006, 7 pp. (pre-publication version of 李锦芳、艾杰瑞 2007 中越红仡佬语比较, 民族语文 2007(3):31-37; Glottolog 321555); archived from ling.uta.edu/~jerry/.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (no 重音/轻声/轻读/弱化). Sec. 一.1 音系: Malipo Red Gelao 5 tones (55, 33, 35, 322, 31), 40 initials, 23 finals, tone sandhi by assimilation; Vietnam Red Gelao 5 tones (44, 31, 13, 35, 31ʔ), 48 initials. Notes prefixes tə-, ka-, a-, ki-, pa-, la- are very frequent and '词头调值不稳定' (prefix tone values are unstable) -- the only prosodic remark about polysyllables. IPA in legacy SIL font extracts garbled; Chinese prose readable.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. & Li Jinfang. [2003/2004]. Red Gelao, the most endangered form of the Gelao language. Unpublished conference/ms. paper, 6 pp. (Glottolog 317732); archived from ling.uta.edu/~jerry/.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'Tones': 'There are four tones in Red Gelao'; C-tone glottal constriction; C-category items change 13->35 in compounds; prenasal onsets resyllabify onto a preceding syllable. Authors state they are 'not presenting a full statement of the sound inventory'. No mention of stress/accent/prominence.

sources.note: Nothing for Gelao/Red Gelao: gives a Red Gelao (Na Khê) wordlist column and says Gelao varieties 'have typically four tones'; the only word-prosody remark ('sesqui-syllabic structure with the first syllable being toneless') is about Buyang, not Gelao.
